description: Deletes a page the way the Pages panel does, in one change: its route (src/routes.tsx on a Xodia template site, the routes file on a React site with routes in code) and its file unless another route uses it, or its .html file on a plain HTML site. The home page stays. The answer lists the files removed and every file that still links to the page (links): fix or remove those links (nav, footer, Link to, a href), then run run_check kind "links". Nothing else is rewritten and no redirect is added: add one for a published page the site no longer needs (skill redirects). The site plan drops the page in the same change. Ask the user before deleting a page they wrote; dryRun says what would go first. Xodia autosaves, so there is no discard: to bring a page back, restore_checkpoint the last restore point from list_checkpoints taken before the delete, or the user restores it in Xodia (Project settings, Activity). Pages with a variable part are not deleted here: a collection's item page goes with its collection (CMS tools), any other one you remove in code. Refused with 409 and action ask_agent when Xodia can't change this site's routes safely (route_shape_unsupported, route_unreadable, delete_unsupported) or the HTML site lists its pages in vite.config (html_pages_listed): then remove it in code yourself. Where delete_page works, never delete a page by editing routes or files by hand. Writes unsaved changes the user reviews and saves in Xodia, and the site plan follows in the same change.

branch.description: Optional branch; default the branch the workspace has open

dryRun.description: Only say which files would go and which pages still link to it; deletes nothing

path.description: The page's address ("/about"), as list_pages shows it

name: delete_page
title: Delete a page
